manifest.title: Zero velocity. Nonzero acceleration.
manifest.summary: A ball tossed straight up beside its velocity-time line. The velocity passes through zero at the top while the slope of the line, the acceleration, stays -g.
assumptions: No air resistance, up is positive.
An idealized vertical throw; real balls feel drag.

plan.title: Zero velocity. Nonzero acceleration.
plan.story:
Maya missed her serve again. The ball had looked still for just long enough to persuade her she could wait. She wanted to know how much time her eyes had actually seen.

Her friend gave her a clue by dropping a ball from his hand. At the instant it came free, its velocity was zero. Gravity was already accelerating it downward. Maya wondered if she could use that same starting point to calculate what happened around the top of her throw.

She took upward as positive and set t = 0 at the highest point. For the calculation, she treated the throw as vertical and ignored air resistance. The ball's weight was F = -m g, so Newton's second law gave her a = F / m = -g, about -9.8 m/s^2. There was no special case in that calculation for the moment when the ball stopped rising.

With zero velocity at t = 0, she could write its velocity and height on either side of the top.

v(t) = -g t, y(t) = y_top - g t^2 / 2.

The velocity told the story she expected. A tenth of a second before the top, it was moving up at about 0.98 m/s. A tenth after, it was moving down at the same speed. The velocity had changed by nearly two metres per second in just a fifth of a second.

The height surprised her. At both those instants, the ball was only 4.9 centimetres below the top. For that whole fifth of a second, it stayed within a space smaller than the width of the ball itself. That was enough to make it look as if it hung there.

On the next serve, she saw the same little hesitation in the air. This time she was already swinging.
plan.cardDescription: At the top, v = 0, but the velocity-time slope stays a = -g. Gravity force is F = mg: more mass, more force, same acceleration. No air resistance.
plan.learningGoal: Explain that the force of gravity is m g and the acceleration is -g at every instant, including the top, so a larger mass changes the force and not the motion.
plan.instructions: Change launch speed or gravity, then press Play. Compare the readings at each pause near the top. Change mass while paused to compare force and acceleration. Press Play again or drag the timeline to continue.

scene.description: Two equal-width scenes side by side in one frame. Left, The motion: a ball on a height ruler fixed at 0 to 2.2 m, zero at the launch mark, up positive, with a blue velocity arrow, a separate dashed warm acceleration arrow and a callout beside it reading velocity (m/s), acceleration (m/s^2) and the downward gravitational force (N), plus a state line (Ready to toss, Rising, At the top, Falling, Back at launch height). Right, Velocity over time: the line v = u - g t on fixed scales 0 to 1.8 s and -5.5 to +5.5 m/s, a blue trace up to the current instant, a linked marker, a faint continuation and an orange local segment labelled with the slope a = -g. Ball, marker and readings move together. No snapshot strip.

observations.text: The velocity follows v = u - g t: +0.98, 0.00 and -0.98 m/s at 0.10 s before, at and 0.10 s after the top at 9.8 m/s^2.
The slope of the velocity line is -gravity at every instant, so the acceleration is nonzero at the top.
The force at the top is mass times gravity: 9.8 N at 1.0 kg and 29.4 N at 3.0 kg, while the trajectory and the velocity graph stay identical.
A faster toss or a weaker gravity moves the top later and higher on the fixed scales.

mode.initialState: Launch speed 4.0 m/s, gravity 9.8 m/s^2, mass 1.0 kg; the ball at the launch mark, time 0.000 s, paused.

controls.label: Play
controls.purpose: Run the motion and replay it.
controls.selectionReason: Time explains the change, and the one supported transport drives every linked view.

controls.label: Time since launch
controls.purpose: Inspect any instant of the motion.
controls.selectionReason: A scrubber lets the learner stop on the instants the explanation compares.

controls.label: Launch speed
controls.purpose: See how the speed of the toss moves the top without changing what gravity does there.
controls.selectionReason: The speed varies continuously and intermediate speeds show that the top moves while the pull does not; two named cases would hide that.

controls.label: Gravity
controls.purpose: See that a different gravity changes the acceleration and the time to the top, not the idea.
controls.selectionReason: Gravity varies continuously and the learner can compare nearby values; two planets would hide that.

controls.label: Mass
controls.purpose: See that mass changes the force of gravity and leaves the acceleration and the motion unchanged.
controls.selectionReason: The mass varies continuously, and the learner changes it while paused at the top to compare force and acceleration at the same instant.

controls.label: At top
controls.purpose: Jump to the top of the toss and pause there.
controls.selectionReason: The top is the one instant the explanation is about; a button reaches it exactly, which dragging the scrubber does not.
controls.effect: Seeks the top marker and pauses.

controls.label: Reset experiment
controls.selectionReason: Replay keeps the settings; Reset restores them so the learner can start over.
controls.effect: Restores launch speed 4.0 m/s, gravity 9.8 m/s^2, mass 1.0 kg and time 0, paused.

assumptions: No air resistance, up is positive.
limitations: An idealized vertical throw; real balls feel drag.

claims.text: The gravitational force is m g and the acceleration is -g at every instant, so doubling the mass doubles the force and leaves the motion unchanged.
claims.check: a = F / m = -m g / m = -g; v = u - g t and y = u t - g t^2 / 2 do not contain m.

findings.message: The layout says the default inputs read 0 to 0.816327 s. The scheduled states use launch speed 4 and gravity 9.8, and the card ends at 0.816327 s, which matches that range. The plan's observation text and the description both cite 0.98 m/s at 0.10 s before the top, and the cp-before capture shows 0.98 m/s at t=0.308163 s. That matches. Even so, the start state does not match the plan's default launch-speed quantities and the 'launch speed 2/5' scrubber examples. This is only a mild concern.

The ball is drawn at y=85.38 with the height axis at 360 and length 290 for 0 to 2.2 m. Height 2.0833 m gives y=360-2.0833*131.8=85.4, which is correct. The callout boxes were placed at y=62 to 146 and the ball is near the top of the scene. The acceleration arrow length is 24 px at g=6, against 39.2 px at g=9.8, so it scales with g. That is fine. However, the velocity arrow and the 'v' label are absent at the top, which is acceptable. The velocity readout is 0. The callout texts (velocity, acceleration and force values) are not exposed in the frames, so I cannot verify the callout content or the claim that the force is shown as a downward gravitational force.

The frames show the callout only as empty boxes. The readout values live in the traces, but the drawn callout text cannot be judged from what I was shown. The callout widens from 156 to 166 px at 29.4 N, which is plausible. The velocity-time graph geometry looks consistent: the marker sits on the zero line at the top.
